Global Nourish Corp - Q3 FY2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Nourish Corp Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you're using a landline or the "raise hand" button if you're using the webcast to ask a question. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins (Vice President of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Nourish Corp's Q3 FY2024 results. Joining me on the call are Mark Ellison, Chief Executive Officer; Jane Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Growth Officer; and David Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Mark Ellison.

Mark Ellison (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 FY2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on five key areas: overall company performance highlights, discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies, impact of new product innovations and launches, organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter and year, and market share trends for major brands.

To dive deeper into these, I'll turn it over to Jane Ramirez, our CFO, who will walk us through the details.

Jane Ramirez (CFO):
Thank you, Mark, and good morning, everyone. Let's start with the overall company performance highlights for the quarter ended September 30, 2024, which really showcase the resilience and momentum across our Food & Beverage portfolio in this dynamic macroeconomic environment.

On the top line, we delivered consolidated net revenues of $14.8 billion, up 9% year-over-year, or 6% on an organic basis excluding FX and acquisitions. This is our 11th straight quarter of organic top-line growth, powered by 4% volume growth and 2% price/mix. Our premiumization strategy continues to shine, steering consumers to higher-margin items such as Zest Zero-Sugar sparkling waters and PlantPower plant-based yogurts. Volumes reflect share gains in core categories, with North American beverages up 7% organically, surpassing peers like Coca-Cola and PepsiCo, thanks to surging demand for functional beverages like electrolyte hydration packs reminiscent of Prime or advanced Gatorade options.

Adjusted EBITDA reached $3.4 billion, with a 180-basis-point expansion to 23% margins—our best Q3 in five years. This came from tight cost controls, including $250 million in gross productivity savings via supply chain tweaks, like new aseptic packaging at our Georgia facility that cut PET bottle material costs by 15%. Gross margins grew 220 basis points to 38.5%, even with cocoa up 25% YoY and dairy up 10%. We countered with hedges covering 70% of 2024 cocoa needs at good rates and rationalized 12% of low-velocity legacy SKUs, much like Mondelez's approach.

Diluted adjusted EPS hit $1.92, up 14% year-over-year and above our guidance midpoint. Free cash flow was outstanding at $2.1 billion, up 20%, funding $1.2 billion in share repurchases and a 10% increase to our quarterly dividend at $0.85 per share—marking our 28th straight annual hike. Our balance sheet is solid, with net debt to EBITDA at 2.1x, leaving plenty of room for M&A; we just closed the $1.75 billion EuroSnack Innovations deal, strengthening savory snacks in EMEA with brands like CrunchWave crisps.

By segment, Beverages—40% of revenues—grew 10% organically to $5.9 billion. Carbonated soft drinks held at +2% volumes with nostalgic relaunches like FizzClassic in retro packaging, but non-carb stole the show: functional waters and RTD coffees up 18% on health trends. HydraBoost, with adaptogens, grabbed 3 points of U.S. market share per Nielsen, similar to Celsius or Olipop. Snacks & Confectionery, 35% of mix, rose 7% organically to $5.2 billion, led by 12% gains in premium nuts and protein bars amid snacking trends—U.S. at-home volumes up 5% per IRI. We managed cocoa inflation with forward contracts and palm oil efficiencies, keeping EBITDA margins at 22%. Convenience Foods, 25%, hit $3.7 billion, up 5% organically; SteamFresh ready-to-eat bowls rode e-commerce growth to 15% of segment sales from 8% last year.

Regionally, North America—55% of revenues—posted 8% organic growth to $8.1 billion, with market share up 1.2 points to 14.5% in IRI channels. Health focus is huge: low/no-sugar SKUs now 35% of beverage sales, from 25% in FY2023. EMEA grew 12% organically to $3.2 billion, driven by 15% volume jumps in plant-based dairy alternatives in the UK and Germany, aided by EU Green Deal tailwinds for oat milk. APAC accelerated 14% organically to $2.2 billion, powered by India and Southeast Asia with hydration sachets and local flavors like mango-lassi RTDs amid urbanization and middle-class expansion—volumes tripled GDP growth. LATAM grew 9% to $1.3 billion despite Brazil FX issues; AmpUp energy drinks took share from local Red Bulls.

Strategically, we're emphasizing innovation-led growth, sustainability, and digital transformation. R&D spend was $450 million this quarter, or 3% of sales, launching 25 new SKUs like keto-friendly NutriCrunch bars with 15g protein from regenerative almonds, eyeing the $100 billion functional food market at 8% CAGR per Euromonitor. On sustainability, Scope 1 & 2 emissions dropped 25% YoY with solar at 12 plants and 100% recyclable packaging on core brands—68% of millennials prioritize ESG per our surveys, like Unilever's Dove. Digitally, our AI demand sensing with IBM Watson hit 92% forecast accuracy, slashing inventory 18% for just-in-time production like Nestlé.

Challenges include commodity swings—wheat up 8% on Black Sea issues—and U.S. labor wage inflation at 5%. But 2024 guidance stands: 5-7% organic revenue growth, adjusted EPS $7.40-$7.60, EBITDA margins at 23%. Q4 catalysts like holiday premiums and EuroSnack integration set us up to beat consensus flat industry growth.

Building on these highlights, let's discuss our pricing actions and revenue growth management—or RGM—strategies, which fueled much of this quarter's success. RGM is our structured approach to topline maximization via pricing, volume, mix, and innovation. We used data-driven pricing and portfolio tweaks to handle input inflation in cocoa, sugar, and dairy while keeping loyalty and share.

Pricing realization was 6.1% globally in Q3, up from 4.8% in Q2 and above peers' 4-5% like PepsiCo and Mondelez. Targeted list price hikes of 7-9% across categories were offset by flat trade spend at 18.2% of revenue. Gross-to-net was 85%, showing strong execution.

Elasticity was favorable at -0.35 versus modeled -0.45—for every 1% price up, volume fell just 0.35%. Premiumization helped: 62% of actions on high-margin items like PureEarth plant-based yogurts and HydraFit low-sugar drinks, where health trends reduce sensitivity. Beverages took 7.2% pricing for 4.1% revenue lift despite 1.2% volume dip, beating NielsenIQ category growth. Snacks saw 5.8% pricing with flat volumes, aided by cocoa-efficient CrunchLite bars offsetting 25% YoY cocoa surge.

By region, North America—52% of revenues—hit 7.5% net pricing, strongest ever, via club channels like Costco. Elasticity -0.25 on staples like FamilyFresh meals. Europe—28%—managed 4.2% amid -0.55 elasticity and HFSS scrutiny; moderated to 5-6% on reformulated items versus Unilever, Danone. Emerging markets—20%—got 6.8% pricing with 3.2% volumes, via VAPs like MegaSip bottles at 12% premium in Brazil, India.

Mix added 1.9% to organic growth, up 40 bps, with 2.5 points shift to premiums: plant-based/functionals now 22% of beverages, 15% higher margins. We optimized 12 portfolios, axing 8% low-velocity SKUs like sugary cereals for RTD coffee, up 28% like Starbucks, Nestlé trends.

Our PriceOptix AI platform covers 85% of 150,000+ SKUs, using IRI/Circana data for ZIP-level elasticity and simulations—like 2% U.S. Midwest lift on hydration promos during heatwaves. Piloting blockchain for EcoHarvest cocoa premiums of 8-10% in Europe, meeting deforestation regs and ESG demand.

For FY24, RGM targets 7-9% organic growth: 5-7% pricing, elasticity under -0.4 via 1,200 extra U.S. grocery feet. Pipeline has 25 SKUs like fiber snacks for gut health, e-comm to 12% sales with 15% higher ASPs on Amazon DTC. Costs like dairy +8%, packaging +6% watched, but we pass 80-90% through pricing, growing volumes 1-2%, lifting ROIC to 14.5% from 13.2%.

A key driver here was the impact of new product innovations and launches. Amid industry volumes down 2.1% per Nielsen and inflation on staples, our NPD drove 18% of 7.2% YoY top-line growth to $2.8 billion in Q3 revenues—wait, aligning with our broader $14.8 billion print.

Innovation pillars: health & wellness, sustainability, convenience. $450 million YTD R&D, up 12%, on precision fermentation, upcycled ingredients, AI flavor profiling—cutting go-to-market to 12 months.

In Beverages—45% revenue—AquaVita+, zero-sugar electrolyte RTD with adaptogens, added $120 million incremental sales via Q3, grabbing 4.2% share in $15B enhanced water per IRI. Velocity 2.5x category, 65% ACV in nine months like early Celsius. $2.49/16oz pricing, 52% margins via ASEAN upcycled coconut co-packers. North America 70% uptake on Gen Z mood-boost prefs (35% per Mintel), APAC pilots $15 million with 25% repeats.

Snacks: GreenBite Plant-Powered Bars with pea protein, high-fiber, 10g protein, regenerative oats—$85 million Q3, 150% QoQ acceleration, 11% segment growth. 1.8 points share in $12B protein bars via clean-label, IBM Food Trust traceability. EMEA 40% sales on UK/Germany flexitarian rise (28% Kantar). 48% margins despite cocoa +7%, hedging 80%, rationalizing 15% legacy.

Dairy alts: NutriOat Creamer oat-based, $65 million via Kroger/Albertsons in 20,000 doors. 22% CAGR non-dairy creamers (Euromonitor), 18% basket uplift with K-cups. China Tmall 30% attach to RTD coffees vs. 5% deflation.

Tech: $100M FlavorForge AI Lab cuts flops 40% to 15%. Enzymatic hydrolysis saves 30% water in proteins, Regenerative Organic certified—62% EMEA priority (NielsenIQ). Precision fermentation with Perfect Day for dairy-free casein, 10% NutriOat by year-end.

Regions: North America (55%) innovations offset 1% legacy dip for 9% growth amid tariffs. EMEA (25%) +14%, GreenBite 20% Scandinavia penetration despite UK HFSS taxes. APAC (15%) +12% on AquaVita+ India (15% hydration CAGR), 70% local sourcing vs. China scrutiny. LatAm pilots $10M on upcycled fruits vs. El Niño.

Our "Innovate or Abdicate" culls 200 low-velocity SKUs, reallocates $150M to NPD—ROIC 25% vs. 14% average, LTV 3x CAC via AR loyalty apps. Beats PepsiCo's 10% NPD (Poppi), Nestlé 12% (Vital Proteins) for FY24 outperformance.

Q4 pipeline: ImmuBoost probiotic gummies for $8B immunity, EcoCrunch chips from brewery grains—20-22% FY24 growth contribution, supporting +6-8% revenue, +150bps EBITDA to 22.5%.

Turning to organic sales growth guidance for Q4 ending December 31, 2024, and FY2025. Organic strips FX, M&A like PureBites tuck-in, discontinued ops—core portfolio health in snacks, beverages, nutritionals.

Q3 was 4.2%, beat 2-4% guide, 6% North America beverage volumes offset salty snack softness vs. Walmart/Kroger privates. Pricing +1.5%, lapping 8% prior hikes.

Q4 guide: 3-5% organic. Seasonal holidays boost staples.

Beverages (45%): 4-6%, VitaQuench zero-sugar rollout like Gatorade Fit plant electrolytes, 85% U.S. ACV, +15% repeats on 'Hydrate Smarter'. Europe 2-3% Tesco/Carrefour vs. post-Olympics.

Snacks (35%): 2-4%, NutriCrunch vs. Rhythm Superfoods, +3-5% distro post 15% SKU prune. GLP-1 headwinds offset by 20g protein NutriBars.

Nutritionals (20%): 5-7%, China Tmall 25% e-comm vs. Optifast, LatAm +8% rebound.

Regions: North America (70%) 3-5%, Europe (15%) 2-4% FX neutral, APAC/LATAM (15%) 5-7%. Risks: cocoa +40% like Hershey, U.S. tariffs; 80% hedged.

FY2025: raised to 4-6% from 3-5%, via 'Core Momentum 2026'. Q1 ~3%, accelerates.

Tailwinds: 20 NPD SKUs/nootropics like Celsius, R&D $150M +12% for 25% growth. Pricing 2-3% on elastic like RTD coffee, absorb dairy via partners. Nielsen/IRI 10% health bev share, $400M trade velocity in 7-Eleven/Costco. AI inventory cuts stockouts 30% post-cocoa issues. GreenCore recycled packaging by mid-'25, +12% loyalty.

Headwinds: CPG basket +3% BLS, privates 22% Kantar, remote snacking. Agile with POS/dynamic pricing.

3-5% Q4, 4-6% FY25 vs. 2.5% industry (Circana), mid-single EPS, ROIC 12%.

Finally, market share trends for major brands. Using NielsenIQ, IRI, Circana, we gained 120 bps YoY to 14.8% global F&B share via "Health Forward", amid inflation, health/sustainability shifts, privates/DTC pressure.

F&B grew 3.2% CC, volumes 1.1%. Majors like us, Pepsi Frito-Lay, Coke core, Nestlé confect stable; sugary legacies lost. Privates +60 bps to 18.4% on Walmart/Aldi value. We won velocity: penetration +2.3% to 78%, repeats +4% shopper marketing.

CSDs (22% revenue): +1.2% to 28.5% global vs. Coke flat 32.1%, Dr Pepper -0.4%. North America Zero Sugar/Pure Sparkle +150 bps to 31.2% ACV, 92% c-stores Vistar. Volumes +0.8% vs. cat -1.2%. EMEA +80 bps to 22.4% vs. Red Bull energy, lime zero +15% UK/Germany velocity. APAC +2.1% to 18.9% Thailand/India multipacks. $150M aseptic CapEx cuts waste 12% for wet markets.

NCBs/Functionals +90 bps to 16.7%, NCBs +5.4%. VitalQuench +2.5 pts vs. Gatorade -1.1% to 24.3%, TikTok 28% e-comm velocity. Plant/low-sugar 42% portfolio vs. Tropicana dip. LatAm +3.4% to 12.6% coconut Brazil. China +110 bps to 10.4% TeaVital kombucha Alibaba. Stevia-ferment cuts sugar 85%.

Snacks/Confect: salty +70 bps to 19.3% vs. Lay's 26.8%. CrunchHealth +1.8 pts better-for-you 22%, protein +18g. Vs. Mondelez confect 21.5% -50 bps chocolate to NutriBar fiber/no-sugar. North America +1.4% to 24.1%, IRI +12% pen club. EMEA -20 bps to 15.7% sugar taxes, air-fried +9% France/Spain. APAC vs. Calbee/Want Want 32%, Vietnam JV 5% ramp YE24 Gen Z packs.

Drivers: premiumization 65% $3+ tiers, +220 bps margins 38%. Supply $300M regen ag pea/Ingredion de-risks cocoa/palm vs. Hershey erosion. AI Nielsen trade +15% ROI, omni +22% DoorDash/Instacart. North America 42% gains, APAC/LATAM 8-10% CAGR 1.2B middle class McKinsey.

Risks: privates +100 bps if inflation, HFCS/PFAS regs. Pipeline 10 functionals/mushroom RTD coffee +200 bps next year, M&A like Brazil yerba mate stake.

This positions our brands for outperformance. Net sales were $14.8 billion, up 9% year-over-year or 6% organic. Gross margin 38.5%, hit by commodity inflation but offset by productivity. Operating income strong, EPS $1.92. Cash and securities robust at levels supporting returns. Reaffirming full-year guidance: 5-7% organic growth, EPS $7.40-$7.60.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, thank you. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Emily Carter (JPMorgan):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflationary pressures on commodities like cocoa and dairy on your business?

Mark Ellison (CEO):
Thanks, Emily. We've seen cocoa up 25% and dairy 10% YoY, but proactive hedging—70% of cocoa locked in—and supply chain savings like 15% lower PET costs kept gross margins expanding 220 bps to 38.5%. RGM pricing passed through effectively, with elasticity better than expected at -0.35, and productivity of $250 million more than offset. We're positioned well heading into Q4.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Rivera with Barclays. Please proceed.

Mike Rivera (Barclays):
What are your plans for AquaVita+ and what is the expected sales contribution going forward?

Lisa Chen (Chief Growth Officer):
Good question, Mike. AquaVita+ has been a standout, generating $120 million incremental through Q3 with 4.2% share in enhanced waters. Plans include national expansion, more co-packer capacity for upcycled ingredients, and APAC scaling where pilots hit 25% repeats. Expect 20-22% of FY24 growth from innovations like this, supporting raised revenue outlook.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

Laura Kim (Morgan Stanley):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

David Patel (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Thanks, Laura. We've diversified sourcing—West Africa alts for cocoa, regen ag partnerships—and AI demand sensing for 92% accuracy, cutting inventory 18% and stockouts 30%. Aseptic lines and $300 million CapEx de-risk volatility like Black Sea wheat or El Niño. EuroSnack integration adds resilience in EMEA. This supports our productivity savings and just-in-time model.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Tom Hale with Deutsche Bank. Please proceed.

Tom Hale (Deutsche Bank):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Jane Ramirez (CFO):
Appreciate it, Tom. Q4 organic 3-5%, driven by holidays, VitaQuench rollout, and premiums. Full-year reaffirmed at 5-7% organic, EPS $7.40-7.60, margins 23%. FY25 raised to 4-6% organic on innovation, pricing discipline, digital shelf gains. Watching inflation and privates, but our flywheel positions us to outperform.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Mark Ellison for closing remarks.

Mark Ellison (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in Global Nourish Corp. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
